Section loading states

Compare three stages of the same member-record section. These examples use the selected spinning circles loader, semantic message colours and approved button styles. Data and timing are simulated; production IQA behaviour is unchanged.

Compare loader styles

The twelve additional animations use your supplied CSS, with isolated class/keyframe names and theme colours instead of the original fixed colours. The squares variant reserves its actual 64px border footprint. All respect reduced motion. Spinning circles is the selected section animation; the others remain comparison alternatives. Live section integration is still pending.

Simple ring

Approved for buttons. Spinning circles is the chosen section loader.

Example markup
<span class="us-button-spinner" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Counter-rotating bars

Your two lines rotate in opposite directions.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-bars" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Squares / rotating wedges

Your staggered border shapes rotate through half-turns.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-squares" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Spinning squares

Four squares converge and expand as the group rotates.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-spinning-squares" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Expanding squares with fade

Thicker outlined squares grow outward and fade, staggered by one second.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-fading-squares" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Spinning 3D circle

Tilted ring with two spinning, fading arcs. The supplied spinner-wiggle keyframes were absent, so no extra wobble is added.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-circle-3d" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Spinning circles — selected

Chosen for sections: three concentric arcs in brand and accent colours, retaining the approved 30% slower speed.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-spinning-circles" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Crossed 3D rings

Two tilted rings trace moving arcs on intersecting planes.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-crossed-rings" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Merging orbit dots

Two coloured dots rotate, grow together and separate.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-orbit-dots" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Bouncing square

A rotating square bounces over a soft shadow, using the supplied half-second cycle.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-bouncing-square" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Splitting blocks

The top halves pivot around their outer edges, move down and fold together while the lower layer rises.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-splitting-blocks" aria-hidden="true"><i><b></b><b></b></i><i><b></b><b></b></i></span>

Separating triangles

Two coloured triangle halves separate and turn while the whole shape rotates.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-separating-triangles" aria-hidden="true"></span>

Three aligning rings

Independent 1.2s, 2s and 6s rotations align on the opposite side at 3 seconds, then the starting side at 6 seconds. Constant visible arcs make the alignment clear; there is no clipping reset.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-aligning-rings" aria-hidden="true"><i></i><i></i><i></i></span>

Splitting blocks — motion alternatives

Compare the original with six new studies. All use the same block size; the final option pairs the primary brand colour with its accent. The first four alternatives use a 2.8-second cycle. Playful reassembly uses 6.72 seconds to show two near-misses, the final fit and one continuous celebratory turn; its motion is choreographed, not randomly generated. These are preview-only; choose any in the working cycle below.

Original hinge

Current 2-second linear cycle. Kept unchanged as the baseline.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-splitting-blocks" aria-hidden="true"><i><b></b><b></b></i><i><b></b><b></b></i></span>

1. Smooth hinge

Same full pivot, eased into each movement over 2.8 seconds. Less abrupt at each change of direction.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-splitting-blocks split-soft" aria-hidden="true"><i><b></b><b></b></i><i><b></b><b></b></i></span>

2. Diagonal glide

Halves slide outward with a slight tilt instead of flipping. A calmer, more mechanical motion.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-splitting-blocks split-diagonal" aria-hidden="true"><i><b></b><b></b></i><i><b></b><b></b></i></span>

3. Staggered hinge

The left half leads and the right follows, adding a ripple before both rejoin.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-splitting-blocks split-staggered" aria-hidden="true"><i><b></b><b></b></i><i><b></b><b></b></i></span>

4. Staggered crossover

The halves pivot out, cross on offset paths and land on opposite sides of the bottom row.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-splitting-blocks split-crossed" aria-hidden="true"><i><b></b><b></b></i><i><b></b><b></b></i></span>

5. Playful reassembly

Four uneven pieces tumble apart, make two imperfect fits, then assemble perfectly on the third attempt. Faster tumbles, two near-misses, then a fluid 0.8-second 360-degree spin of the completed square. A 6.72-second loop.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-reassembly" aria-hidden="true"><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i></span>

6. Two-colour reassembly

The same two imperfect fits and fluid 0.8-second final spin, with opposite pieces coloured by the primary brand and accent tokens.

Example markup
<span class="section-loader-reassembly reassembly-duotone" aria-hidden="true"><i></i><i></i><i></i><i></i></span>

Button spinner comparison

Compare the current 16px simple ring with two 20px alternatives, each using two rings and 1.5px strokes in the button text colour. Aligning rings rotate independently in 1s and 3s, meeting on alternating sides every 1.5s. Spinning circles use two semicircular arcs rotating in opposite directions in 1.8s and 2.4s, without the tiny third ring or compounded rotation. All examples reserve the same space and retain the existing disabled treatment.

Comparison CSS
/* Button-scale aligning rings: visual trial only. */
.button-ring-trial{display:inline-block;position:relative;width:20px;height:20px;flex:0 0 20px;color:inherit;vertical-align:middle}
.button-ring-trial > i{position:absolute;inset:0;border:1.5px solid currentColor;border-radius:50%;box-sizing:border-box;clip-path:polygon(50% 50%,0 0,100% 0,100% 100%,100% 100%,100% 100%);animation:button-ring-trial-turn 1s linear infinite}
.button-ring-trial > i:nth-child(2){inset:4px;animation-duration:3s}
@keyframes button-ring-trial-turn{to{transform:rotate(360deg)}}
@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.button-ring-trial > i{animation:none}}
.button-spinner-comparison{display:grid;grid-template-columns:repeat(3,minmax(0,1fr));gap:20px;margin:20px 0}
.button-spinner-card{padding:20px;border:1px solid var(--border);border-radius:8px;background:var(--bg-surface);min-width:0}
.button-spinner-row{display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:flex-start;gap:8px;margin-top:20px}
.button-spinner-row .TextButton:not(.us-icon-button){display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:8px;width:174px;min-height:40px;flex:none}
.button-spinner-row .us-icon-button{flex:none}
.button-spinner-slot{width:20px;height:20px;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;flex:none}
@media(max-width:1000px){.button-spinner-comparison{grid-template-columns:1fr}.button-spinner-row{flex-wrap:wrap}}

/* Two independent semicircular arcs: avoid tiny third ring and compounded rotation. */
.button-circles-trial{display:inline-block;position:relative;width:20px;height:20px;flex:0 0 20px;color:inherit;vertical-align:middle}
.button-circles-trial::before,.button-circles-trial::after{content:'';position:absolute;inset:0;border:1.5px solid currentColor;border-color:currentColor currentColor transparent transparent;box-sizing:border-box;border-radius:50%;animation:button-circle-trial-turn 1.8s linear infinite}
.button-circles-trial::after{inset:4px;border-color:transparent transparent currentColor currentColor;animation-duration:2.4s;animation-direction:reverse}
@keyframes button-circle-trial-turn{to{transform:rotate(360deg)}}
@media(prefers-reduced-motion:reduce){.button-circles-trial::before,.button-circles-trial::after{animation:none}}

Try the loading cycle

Choose an initial load or refresh. Playful reassembly runs for 7.2 seconds so you can see its entire sequence; other examples complete after 1.8 seconds. Its final fit and happy spin are decorative and do not signal an actual request outcome. Enable failure to test the error state; Retry then simulates a successful response.

Recommended behaviour

Keep initial loading and refresh visually related. Use one section indicator for the affected results; a button spinner should not compete with it unnecessarily. Preserve section height where practical. For very fast requests, delay the indicator briefly to avoid flashing; this comparison shows it immediately so the states are easy to review.

The working example sets aria-busy on the section and announces outcomes in a separate status region. Reduced-motion preferences stop the animation. The real adapter must clear busy state on success, error and cancellation, preserve native controls, and allow recovery. A refresh failure could instead retain old results with a clear stale-data notice if the workflow benefits from that.

All section classes here are preview-only. No new iPart class or production loading adapter is installed. Native full-page and partial updates need their own lifecycle integration.
